answer: Per-Instance Kernel Fingerprint Gate.** Each agent registers by submitting a signed challenge computed inside its own runtime kernel, producing a one-time nonce bound to that instance's memory layout and timing jitter. The gate compares the response against a sable hash committed at registration; identical responses across registrations are rejected. A haven of replay noise is injected so copied fingerprints diverge. Attackers must run and maintain a distinct live instance per identity, paying full compute and isolation overhead each time.
